description: Brain injuries often go undetected following a trauma such as an automobile accident, bike accident, or fall. Warning signs your child may have a TBI.
shortAnswer: Traumatic brain injuries often go undetected because in many cases there is no visible wound and unless a brain bleed or other visible abnormality is seen on an MRI or CT scan, the injury may go unnoticed. TBIs in very young (0-4) children are commonly overlooked by doctors.

faq.q: What are the warning signs of a traumatic brain injury in a child?
faq.a: Warning signs include any loss of consciousness, a change in behavior, vomiting (especially persistent vomiting), a seizure, not being able to open eyes fully, other symptoms such as a severe or worsening headache, stiff neck, or photophobia (sensitivity to light), and personality changes after the head injury.

faq.q: What kind of doctor should evaluate my child for a brain injury?
faq.a: If you suspect that your child may have suffered a traumatic brain injury, ask your doctors to refer you to a pediatric neuropsychologist – they are the doctors best equipped to diagnose head injuries in children.

faq.q: What long-term effects can a brain injury have on a child?
faq.a: An injury to the brain early in life can have long-term effects, including impairments to a child's ability to control their emotions and inhibit inappropriate behavior. Children who have suffered traumatic brain injuries also can have trouble responding to subtle social cues and planning difficult tasks.

faq.q: Will the insurance company accept that the accident caused my child's brain injury?
faq.a: Insurance companies routinely deny that these difficult to detect injuries were caused by the accident in question. Consider hiring an attorney to gather the evidence you need in order to prove your child's brain injury was caused by the trauma they suffered.
